produces: a cover letter and a statement draft, ready to edit
note: Five questions, asked once per application. Every field the draft asserts traces to an answer here or to a cited record. Nothing is inferred from the operator's history without saying so.

questions.ask: What register — formal institutional, plain direct, or in your own voice?
questions.why: It determines every sentence, and it is the thing a generated draft gets wrong first.

questions.ask: What are you actually applying with — which work, and is it finished?
questions.why: An unfinished work changes the whole pitch from evidence to intention, and the draft has to know which it is making.

questions.ask: What is the constraint they will worry about — budget, timeline, eligibility, or venue?
questions.why: The strongest paragraph in any application answers the reviewer's objection before it is raised.

questions.ask: Is there anything you do NOT want said here?
questions.why: Cheaper to ask than to retract. Employment matters, unpublished work, anything under embargo.

questions.ask: Should the draft cite the sourced article we found, or leave it out?
questions.why: The citation is real and named. Whether it belongs in this letter is a judgement about the reader, and that judgement is yours.

refuses: Inventing an eligibility claim the call does not state
Asserting what will catch a named person's attention as though it were sourced
Filling Q4 by inference from anything in the archive
